Placeholder page. The framing text is a draft; the papers below come from the publications data.
:::

Doctoral fieldwork in Eastern Province, Sierra Leone, between 2020 and 2023.
Repeated trapping at four village sites, along a transect from closed forest
through farm bush to the inside of dwellings, across 43,226 trap nights.

The question underneath all of it: land use decides which small mammals live
where, so does it also decide where *Mammarenavirus lassaense* circulates, and
where people meet it?

## Data and code

Protocols are archived on the Open Science Framework, field data are collected
with Open Data Kit, and analysis code sits in the project repositories. Trapping
records are deposited on GBIF and PHAROS.
